title_zh: 债券的「世代机遇」？——对话 Priya Misra 与 Joanna Gallegos
subtitle_zh: 美债收益率新高下信用市场分化加剧，主动配置收益型固收正当时

turns.en: Welcome to ETF EDGE, the podcast. If you're looking to learn the latest insights on all things exchange-traded funds, you're in the right place.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 ETF Edge 播客。如果你想了解关于交易型开放式指数基金（ETF）的最新洞察，那你可来对地方了。

turns.en: Every week, we're bringing you compelling interviews, thoughtful market analysis, and breaking down what it all means for investors. I'm Brandon Gomez.
turns.zh: 每周我们都会带来精彩的访谈、深度的市场分析，并且为投资者拆解这些动态背后的含义。我是 Brandon Gomez。

turns.en: US treasuries at record highs are stealing the headlines, but there are big shifts also happening in other areas of the credit markets. Here's my conversation with Priya Misra, portfolio manager at JP Morgan Asset Management, along with Joanna Gallegos, bond blocks, co-founder and CEO.
turns.zh: 美国国债收益率屡创新高，抢尽了风头，但信用市场的其他领域同样正在发生重大变化。下面是我与 JP Morgan Asset Management 的基金经理 Priya Misra，以及 Bond Blocks 联合创始人兼 CEO Joanna Gallegos 的对谈。

turns.en: Thank you both for joining me today. So let's get started broadly with US treasuries, right, as those have been the current headline grabber.
turns.zh: 感谢两位今天来到节目。那我们就先从美国国债开始聊起吧，毕竟这是当下最热门的话题。

turns.en: Priya, I want to start the conversation with you because you first, you say that it's the last leg of the move was overdone. Why do you say this?
turns.zh: Priya，我想先请你来谈。你说过这轮走势的最后一段有些过头了，为什么这么说？

turns.en: So I think some of the rise in rates was sort of for good reasons. The economy is extremely resilient, the Fed has started to raise rates, there's an oil price shock, so inflation's a little above target.
turns.zh: 我觉得利率上涨的一部分原因是合理的。经济非常有韧性，美联储已经开始加息了，又有油价冲击，所以通胀略高于目标水平。

turns.en: The last leg of the move, so the last two weeks, there has not been a fundamental catalyst. In fact, I would argue all the economic data over the last two weeks has been actually slightly on the weaker side.
turns.zh: 但最后这段走势——也就是过去两周——并没有基本面的催化剂。实际上我认为过去两周公布的经济数据反而是略微偏弱的。

turns.en: Inflation came in a little bit softer. We had the jobs report that was not weak, but it was not strong. And we're not seeing signs of overheating or demand-led inflation.
turns.zh: 通胀数据稍微温和一些。就业报告不算弱，但也不算强。我们并没有看到经济过热或需求驱动型通胀的迹象。

turns.en: Even Fed officials have come out and said, maybe one or two more rate hikes. The market's pricing in three more rate hikes. So I would argue this last bit is sort of position capitulation, technical factors, there's negative convexity in mortgages.
turns.zh: 甚至美联储官员也出来表态说，可能就再加一到两次。而市场定价反映的是还要再加三次。所以我认为最后这一小段更多是仓位投降、技术性因素——抵押贷款还有负凸性（negative convexity）的问题。

turns.en: I think people are hedging the rate move, and that's why the move looks a little overdone. So we're now thinking duration, which we've not been in duration for a while, starts to make sense to own a little bit, take some duration risk, because that last 25, 30 basis point seems a bit overdone.
turns.zh: 我觉得大家都在对冲利率走势，这就是为什么这轮移动看起来有些过头了。我们现在开始考虑久期（duration），之前我们有一段时间没有配置久期了，现在开始有理由持有一些、承担一些久期风险，因为最后那 25 到 30 个基点似乎有点过度了。

turns.en: And Joanna, I mean, how do you feel about treasury yields hovering around those all-time highs and perhaps some of what Priya just said? Yeah, it depends on where you look.
turns.zh: Joanna，你对国债收益率徘徊在这些历史高位、以及 Priya 刚才所说的那些，怎么看？嗯，这要看你从哪个角度看。

turns.en: Obviously, the duration trade's been very difficult to call over the last three or four years. So we tend to have people focus less on duration and more on income and looking at appropriate spread opportunities across credit.
turns.zh: 显然，过去三到四年久期交易非常难判断。所以我们倾向于让大家少关注久期，多关注收益，以及在整个信用领域寻找合适的利差机会。

turns.en: So in particular, if you can still trade more precisely in this market now, we would suggest something in the investment grade triple B space versus kind of coming all the way into treasury duration to the look for that attractive entry point.
turns.zh: 具体而言，如果你现在能在这个市场更精准地操作，我们建议关注投资级 BBB 板块的机会，而不是一直在国债久期里等到一个诱人的入场点。

turns.en: We say go into more of the corporate credit side in this environment and keep duration as short as you can. We think that's the right way to start considering this market as an entry point.
turns.zh: 我们建议在这种环境下转向企业信用一侧，久期尽量保持短。我们认为这才是把当前市场视为入场起点的正确方式。

turns.en: So if I can add to Joanna there, I would completely agree. We like credit risk as well. But as the AI capex build out is being financed, a lot of that issuance is now out the curve as well.
turns.zh: 如果让我在 Joanna 的基础上补充的话，我完全同意。我们也喜欢信用风险。但随着 AI 资本开支（capex）扩张在融资，很多发行现在也在拉长久期。

turns.en: So we're seeing tenure credit by some of the best companies out there. So, you know, I think it makes sense. We certainly like credit risk. But at some point, you take a little bit of duration along with that credit risk and you can buy 10 year hyperscalar debt or 30 year hyperscalar debt start to just because the curve is now steep and the spread curve is also steep.
turns.zh: 所以我们看到一些最优质公司在发长久期信用债。我觉得这是合理的，我们当然喜欢信用风险，但在某个时点，你在承担信用风险的同时也加入一些久期，就可以去买 10 年期或 30 年期的超大规模云计算商（hyperscaler）债券——因为收益率曲线现在变陡了，信用利差曲线也在变陡。

turns.en: So you're picking up income, but you've also got that potential for capital gain if interest rates stop rising. Well, speaking of rates, I mean, while we're at it, what are your expectations, Priya?
turns.zh: 这样你既能获得收益，如果利率停止上升你还有资本增值的潜力。说到利率，我们趁此问一下，Priya，你的预期是什么？

turns.en: Let's start with you for the Fed's path going forward. I think there's at least one or two more rate hikes. I don't think a lot more very different from 2022 because at that point there was demand lead inflation in the system and they had to hike a lot to really slow things down.
turns.zh: 我们从美联储后续路径开始聊。我觉得至少还有一到两次加息。我认为不会像 2022 年那样大幅加息，因为当时系统里存在需求拉动的通胀，他们必须大幅加息才能真正冷却。

turns.en: Now when we look at the where inflation is coming from, it's coming from tariffs that's leaving the data over the next few months. Oil prices, if oil prices stay here, they actually fall, it's good.
turns.zh: 现在看通胀来源，主要来自关税，这些会在未来几个月逐步消退。油价方面，如果油价维持在这里甚至下跌，那其实是好事。

turns.en: But even if they stay around here, it starts to leave the year-over-year inflation numbers. So I think another hike in October looks a little hard.
turns.zh: 即便油价维持在这个水平，它也会逐步从同比通胀数据中消退。所以我认为 10 月再加息的可能性有点大。

turns.en: We haven't had data that should justify an October hike, but maybe one in December and perhaps one more early on in the year. So they just take the insurance cuts that they put in last year, they take that out.
turns.zh: 我们目前没有能支持 10 月加息的数据，但 12 月可能有一次，也许明年年初还有一次。他们只是把去年加的那些预防性加息——把那些拿掉。

turns.en: But that's it and the markets are more than priced for it. So I think rate hikes are less, should mean less for the long end of the curve. Joanne, are similar expectations or a different take?
turns.zh: 但也就这样了，市场定价已经超额反映了。所以我认为加息次数较少，对曲线长端来说意味着影响更小。Joanna，你的预期类似还是不同？

turns.en: No, I think we, as I mentioned, we think that you should be paying attention to duration and being able to trade into it within these markets.
turns.zh: 不，我觉得我们刚才提到的观点是，你应该关注久期，并且在这些市场中伺机交易久期。

turns.en: We recommend staying away from duration and going more shorter, looking at all the positive things you're seeing in the economy and how, while it's really a rate story that you're seeing some of these changes, you're not seeing broad pressure in corporate credit problems yet.
turns.zh: 我们建议远离久期、保持更短，看看经济中那些积极因素——虽然你看到的这些变化本质上是一个利率故事，但你还没有看到企业信用领域出现普遍性压力。

turns.en: You may see some spots, but that's where you want to really consider getting some corporate debt into your portfolio and taking advantage of, you know, these yields are historically attractive because of the base rates being so high, but they're also incredibly stable because in credit, you know, the fundamentals of these corporations are so strong and the economy continues to grow.
turns.zh: 你可能会看到一些局部情况，但那正是你应该考虑把企业债加入组合、利用这些收益率的时机——因为基准利率很高所以收益率有历史吸引力，但同时信用利差又极其稳定，因为企业基本面很强，经济在持续增长。

turns.en: And so we really think that's being lost in the narrative around treasury rates. You sort of bring up that corporate credit as well. And Priya, I want to ask you about this because you mentioned that while spreads look tight on a historical basis, there's a greater dispersion building under the surface.
turns.zh: 我们真的觉得这一点被国债利率的叙事给淹没了。你刚才也提到了企业信用。Priya，我想就这个问你：你说过虽然利差从历史来看很紧，但水面之下正在出现更大的分化。

turns.en: I mean, for you, what are the clear signs of that? Sure. So if you look within the high yield space, it's very clear triple C spreads are almost a thousand over which typically over treasuries typically happens in a recession.
turns.zh: 对你来说，那些明确的信号是什么？好的。如果你看高收益领域内部，信号非常明显——CCC 级利差已经接近一千个基点，这种水平通常只有在衰退时才会出现。

turns.en: And then you look at double B, single B, and they look, you know, fifth percentile in terms of the historical metrics. So they look really tight.
turns.zh: 然后你再看 BB 级和 B 级，从历史指标看处于第 5 百分位，也就是说利差看起来非常紧。

turns.en: What's happening? I think lower rated companies, companies that might have more debt. You know, when interest rates rise, it's the levered company that companies that start to struggle.
turns.zh: 发生了什么？我觉得是低评级公司、那些杠杆比较高的公司出了问题。利率上升时，最先感到困难的是高杠杆企业。

turns.en: So we're noticing that dispersion. Now the good news back to Joanna's point, you can actually take credit risk in the highest quality companies and still get six and a half percent.
turns.zh: 所以我们注意到了这种分化。好消息是——回到 Joanna 的观点——你可以在最高质量的企业上承担信用风险，仍然拿到 6.5% 的收益率。

turns.en: So you actually don't have to go down in credit, but we're seeing it in high yield. We're even seeing it in investment grade. I mean, investment grade spreads five wider on the year, but you look at the tax sector and they're about 25 wide on the year.
turns.zh: 所以你其实不必下沉信用品质。但我们在高收益领域看到了分化，在投资级里也看到了。投资级利差今年以来走阔了 5 个基点，但你去看市政债板块，已经走阔了大约 25 个基点。

turns.en: So now we can start to say, oh, here's where we can pick up. So I think this is the time for active management. It's very hard to say I like all bonds because you just start looking under the hood.
turns.zh: 所以现在我们可以开始说：哦，机会在这里。我觉得这是主动管理的好时机。你很难再说'我看好所有债券'了，因为你得开始掀开引擎盖看看里面了。

turns.en: Mortgages have been getting crushed because they are very interest rate sensitive. So we start to find opportunities across asset classes. And that dispersion, I think we have not lived in a dispersion world for a while because interest rates were low.
turns.zh: 抵押贷款支持证券被压得很惨，因为它们对利率非常敏感。所以我们开始跨资产类别寻找机会。而这种分化——我觉得我们已经很久没有生活在一个分化的世界里了，因为之前利率太低。

turns.en: Now with base rates where they are, I think you're starting to see opportunities and, you know, we can see where we're getting the best risk adjusted returns.
turns.zh: 现在基准利率到了这个位置，我觉得机会正在显现，我们可以看到哪里能获得最佳的风险调整后回报。

turns.en: I think we've touched on some things, but Joanna, coming back to you, I mean, you mentioned advising clients to focus on income over duration.
turns.zh: 我想我们已经涉及了一些话题。Joanna，回到你这边——你建议客户关注收益而非久期。

turns.en: You've brought that up today already. And corporate credit. I mean, what levels are you still looking at as well when you're making these advisements?
turns.zh: 你今天就这个话题已经提到了。还有企业信用。在做这些建议时，你还在关注哪些具体点位？

turns.en: Yeah, just to put a little color on what Priya just said. So the dispersion and being able to trade precisely across credit ratings, as she just mentioned, and quality.
turns.zh: 好的，我来给 Priya 刚才说的内容加一些具体数字。就是她提到的信用分化，以及在信用评级和品质之间精准交易的能力。

turns.en: So just put some numbers against that. So the triple B's, which is sort of the last credit rating and investment grade, you're getting about 6.2% for that space.
turns.zh: 我列一些数据。BBB 级——算是投资级的最后一个评级档位——收益率大约在 6.2%。

turns.en: If you move over just into double B's, which is the highest quality rung of high yield, you know, double B's are at 7%, single B's are at 8%, and backed up by some of the strength in the fundamentals across the economy.
turns.zh: 如果你再往高收益方向走一点到了 BB 级——这是高收益中质量最好的一档——BB 级收益率在 7%，B 级在 8%，而且背后是整个经济基本面的支撑。

turns.en: That's a real space to consider, especially since in triple B's, you could trade that with short duration. We have a product called triple BS, and it allows you just to precisely grab these opportunities.
turns.zh: 这是一个值得认真考虑的空间。尤其是在 BBB 这个档位，你可以配合短久期来交易。我们有一只产品叫 BBB（Ticker: BSUS），让你可以精准地抓住这些机会。

turns.en: So to Priya's point, at Bomb Blocks, we designed our entire product set for these markets so you can trade that dispersion she's talking about.
turns.zh: 所以用 Priya 的话来说，在 Bond Blocks 我们围绕这类市场设计了整个产品矩阵，让你能够交易她所说的那种分化。

turns.en: And you know, we look at it every day. You can even look at our triple C product and you can watch those spreads develop and you can think about possibly when they get to a high enough level, they may also be a good entry point.
turns.zh: 我们每天都在看。你甚至可以关注我们的 CCC 级产品，看那些利差如何演变——当它们到一个足够高的水平时，可能也是一个不错的入场点。

turns.en: So, you know, just to put the numbers on it so you can see it shine a light on it. I think that's the real hope and opportunity that we're really pushing investors to start taking a look at.
turns.zh: 所以我把数字摆出来，让大家看到这些机会。我觉得这才是我们真正在推动投资者去关注的希望和机遇。

turns.en: That's great to highlight too, the Bomb Blocks products. I mean, Priya, specifically with the funds that you're managing, how are you adjusting your allocations right now when it comes to everything that we're talking about today?
turns.zh: 提到 Bond Blocks 的产品也很好。Priya，具体到你管理的基金，对于我们今天讨论的这些内容，你目前正在怎么调整配置？

turns.en: Sure. We have that I work on, JCPB, it's Core Plus, so it's multi-sector, it's got credit, it's got duration, it's got, you know, mortgages.
turns.zh: 好的。我管理的其中一只是 JCPB，它是核心增强（core plus）策略，所以是多板块的——有信用、有久期、也有抵押贷款。

turns.en: And so what we're doing is we are looking under the hood, bond by bond, sub-sector by sub-sector to see where is the opportunity exactly to join us point.
turns.zh: 我们正在做的就是逐债、逐子板块地掀开引擎盖，看看机会到底在哪里——就像刚才提到的那样。

turns.en: We've actually been increasing some of the double B single B exposure because there has been a widening in high yield spreads. I think it's just been dragged along with, you know, general spread widening in the triple C.
turns.zh: 实际上我们一直在增加一些 BB 和 B 级的敞口，因为高收益利差走阔了。我觉得主要是被 CCC 级利差走阔带下去的。

turns.en: We've been adding some high quality high yield. We like some investment grade and now we've started in the last few days to increase some duration as well thinking we may be nearing the end of that rate move.
turns.zh: 我们一直在配置一些高评级高收益债，也看好一些投资级，而且最近几天我们已经开始增加一些久期了，因为我们觉得利率这轮走势可能接近尾声了。

turns.en: So I think having diversified sources of alpha in a portfolio just allows you to position for, it's a resilient economy, but every time the bond market speaks, I think other markets need to start to pay attention at some point or something break and we just saw what happened with Europe, you know, is the housing market next you to drop.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得在组合里保持多元化的 alpha 来源，能让你更好地定位——经济有韧性没错，但每当债市发出信号，我觉得其他市场最终都得开始关注，否则就会出问题。我们刚看到欧洲的情况——下一个是房市吗？

turns.en: So I think to be very thoughtful about sizing of these positions and to have this diversified set of alpha or set of risk factors in a portfolio, we think makes sense.
turns.zh: 所以我认为对这些仓位做好规模管理、保持一组多元化的 alpha 来源或风险因子在组合中，是有道理的。

turns.en: Yeah. Which of the, I mean, there's are so many macro factors at play when you're making these types of decisions and you sort of listed some of them in terms of different industries and factors, but like if I'm trying to figure out the long-term strategy play here, Priya, what am I focusing in on the most?
turns.zh: 嗯。你刚才列了一些——做这类决策时有那么多宏观因素在起作用，你提到了不同行业和因子。但比如如果我想要搞清楚长期的策略布局，Priya，我应该最关注什么？

turns.en: I think it's income, so fixed income is giving you that income, it's giving you real income. Like one thing we should note, this rise in rates has all been a real rate lead move, not inflation.
turns.zh: 我觉得是收益。固定收益给你的是收益，是真实收益。有一点我们值得注意：这轮利率上升完全是实际利率驱动的，不是通胀。

turns.en: So where fixed income becomes a little scary back to 2022, we all have PTSD from there, was because I was inflation led and the Fed had to raise a lot of rates.
turns.zh: 固定收益什么时候会变得让人害怕呢——回到 2022 年，大家对那段时间都有点创伤后应激了——那是因为当时是通胀驱动，美联储不得不大幅加息。

turns.en: So I think having a macro view, is this a real rate lead move? Am I picking up real return and then to look at what part of the economy might be susceptible or vulnerable to this and making sure that we stay away from those sectors.
turns.zh: 所以我认为拥有一个宏观视角很重要：这是不是一轮实际利率驱动的上升？我是否在获取真实回报？然后看看经济的哪些部分可能对此比较脆弱，确保我们远离那些板块。

turns.en: So some lower end consumer ABS, subprime auto, that's the sector that, you know, hard to know at what rate level does that sector struggle, but we might be getting close to that.
turns.zh: 比如一些低端消费者资产支持证券（ABS）、次级车贷——这个板块你很难说利率到什么水平它才会出问题，但我们可能正在接近那个临界点。

turns.en: So trying to reduce our exposure there and increase our exposure to the AI trade, where I think the price sensitivity of those issuers is much less and they have barely any turn of leverage.
turns.zh: 所以我们试图减少那里的敞口，增加对 AI 主线的配置。因为我觉得那些发行人的价格敏感度要低得多，而且他们几乎没有杠杆。

turns.en: I mean, they're not even one turn of leverage, you know, a lot of the AI companies. So increasing our credit risk in those sectors, reducing maybe the consumer housing, unless you know, there's a lot of baby being thrown out of the bathwater along with the bathwater, then you can say, okay, there's too much cheapening in one sector and that's when we can step in.
turns.zh: 我是说很多 AI 公司连一轮杠杆都不到。所以我们在这些板块增加信用风险敞口，减少消费和住房类的配置——除非确实出现把婴儿连同洗澡水一起倒掉的情况，某个板块被过度打压了，那时候我们可以进场。

turns.en: So I think you want to be looking bond by bond and sort of sector by sector to see where the macro and you have to do the bottom up as well to make sure that companies are not over-leveled.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得你要逐债、逐板块地去看，找到宏观层面的机会。同时也必须做自下而上的分析，确保公司没有被过度加杠杆。

turns.en: Joe and I would just be curious to sort of get your take as well. I mean, outside of the ones that you've mentioned already, which other bomb blocks we eat of products, are you most recommending clients specifically focus on now?
turns.zh: 我们也很好奇 Joanna 你怎么看。除了你刚才提到的那些之外，目前你最推荐客户关注 Bond Blocks 哪些 ETF 产品？

turns.en: Yeah. So again, the theme that Priya and I are hitting on is that it's really in the investor's best interest to start looking at the income that's back in fixed income.
turns.zh: 好的。我和 Priya 一直在反复说的主题是：现在真的到了投资者该关注固定收益重新回归的收益的时候了。

turns.en: Take an offset the volatility in your portfolio and also to think about how you want to compose that income in your portfolio. So another area we look at is, you know, asking people to pay attention to the duration risk of course being low and thinking about what you're getting for that yield.
turns.zh: 用这些收益来对冲组合中的波动，同时也想一想你希望怎么构建组合中的收入来源。另一个我们关注的领域是：虽然久期风险当然不能忽视，但要想清楚你为了收益率得到了什么。

turns.en: So when you can play with these ratings, you can play with duration. We really like our private credit ETF as well. It yields near 7%, it has a lot of diversification because it uses CLOs, but you're getting an incredible amount of yield for very, very low volatility and investors really like that space because that's what they're doing in the treasury space, that's what they're doing in the credit space.
turns.zh: 当你能在不同评级之间灵活操作、在久期上灵活操作时，选择就多了。我们也非常喜欢我们的私募信用 ETF——收益率接近 7%，因为使用了贷款抵押债券（CLO）所以分散化程度很高，而且你在非常非常低的波动率下就能获得极高的收益。投资者真的很喜欢这个领域，因为他们在国债和信用市场做的就是同样的事。

turns.en: They're trying to reduce down certain factors of risk without forsaking other things like yield and potential return. And I want to note just one thing about bonds in general.
turns.zh: 他们试图降低某些风险因子，同时不放弃收益和潜在回报这些方面。我还想就债券整体补充一点。

turns.en: This month was one of the first months where fixed income flows in ETFs surpassed equity flows in ETFs. So just to really put it in there for bonds are back and bonds are really important.
turns.zh: 本月是固定收益 ETF 的资金流入首次超过股票 ETF 资金流入的月份之一。所以这真的说明：债券回来了，而且债券真的很重要。

turns.en: I think that investor sentiment of reallocating back into or increasing their allocations, updating their allocations in their bond portfolios across core products and core plus products and also all of these different points of differentiating we're talking about is starting to show in the flows quite a bit.
turns.zh: 我觉得投资者情绪的转变——重新配置回债券组合、增加配置比例、在核心产品和核心增强产品之间以及我们讨论的这些差异化领域进行更新——已经在资金流中体现出来了。

turns.en: That's a great point. If I can jump in, the fact that there have been all these inflows coming in, so much is being talked about supply, government supply, global government supply with defense, with energy security, AI supply, there's a demand side that's actually meeting this supply.
turns.zh: 说得好。如果我能插一句的话，这么多资金流入进来，大家都在讨论供给——政府供给、全球政府债券供给、防务、能源安全、AI 相关供给——但其实有一个需求端正在承接这些供给。

turns.en: And that's why, yes, interest rates have gone up, but credit spreads have been remarkably well behaved. I think it's because investors are looking at these level of yields and saying, maybe we do get diversification and income from fixed income and they're piling into bonds.
turns.zh: 这就是为什么利率虽然上升了，但信用利差表现得出奇地稳定。我觉得是因为投资者看到这些收益率水平后在说：也许我们确实可以从固定收益中获得分散化和收益，于是他们大举涌入债券。

turns.en: But the other point I would make is active and I think Joanna and I both talking about that the need to be active with your fixed income allocation because you want to be careful about duration.
turns.zh: 但我想补充的另一点是主动管理。我和 Joanna 都谈到了在固定收益配置中需要主动管理，因为你要小心久期。

turns.en: If you're just in an index product, you might have more duration than you want or you need or you know that you have and to be careful about which sectors are you buying and not just taking index level risk because it's the highest, most debted companies, that'll be the largest weight in the index.
turns.zh: 如果你只持有一个指数产品，你可能持有了比你想要的或需要的更多的久期。而且你要小心自己在买哪些板块——不要只吃指数层面的风险，因为指数里权重最大的往往是负债最多的公司。

turns.en: And you may not want the most exposure to the most debted governments or companies. So I think just being active in fixed income is another trend that we're noticing.
turns.zh: 而你未必想要对负债最高的政府或公司有最大敞口。所以我觉得固定收益中主动管理是我们在观察到的另一个趋势。

turns.en: I mean, definitely hand selecting, right, those that exposure. I mean, while we have you both more of an ETF industry question, which I think we're kind of picking at a little bit, but Joanna, I'll start with you.
turns.zh: 确实，精选持仓很重要。趁两位都在，我想问一个关于 ETF 行业的问题——我们之前多少也在触及这个话题。Joanna，我先问你。

turns.en: I mean, we've seen a massive amount of product innovation on the equity side of things. I mean, could we expect more bond related products in the near future?
turns.zh: 我们在股票端已经看到了大量的产品创新。那么在债券相关产品上，未来我们能否期待更多新品面世？

turns.en: Absolutely, because I think there's an insatiable need for income. And so you're seeing development across fixed income in many ways from many providers that can be really important to investors to have a lot of choice.
turns.zh: 绝对可以，因为我觉得市场对收益的需求是无止境的。你会看到很多固定收益领域的新开发——来自不同发行方、以各种方式呈现——对投资者来说，有丰富的选择权真的很重要。

turns.en: You're going to see things in more granular cuts like we do here at bomb blocks. You're going to see things that are going to deliver you an outcome in income, maybe by use of derivatives.
turns.zh: 你会看到更细分的产品——就像我们在 Bond Blocks 做的这种。你还会看到通过衍生品来交付收益结果的产品。

turns.en: But the most important thing is, you know, for years and years and years, I think the fixed income space in ETFs, one of the premises of why bomb blocks exist today was underdeveloped and we're seeing new heights in the AUM for fixed income ETFs overall.
turns.zh: 但最重要的是——多年来，我认为 ETF 中的固定收益领域一直是欠发达的。Bond Blocks 存在的前提之一就是这个领域被忽视了。而现在我们看到固定收益 ETF 的整体资产管理规模正在创新高。

turns.en: The projections for fixed income growth into 2030 are actually in the way we look at the market and the way we've analyzed it. You're kind of on a faster clip if you were to make all things equal than equities themselves.
turns.zh: 到 2030 年固定收益增长的预测——按照我们分析和看待市场的方式——如果在同等条件下比较，增速其实比股票还要快。

turns.en: So we're going to see many, many people and many, many products come to market, many, many issuers and many products come to market to help people make sense of the new dynamics in the market, the more precision and information that people have in order to construct their portfolio or even just respond to volatility, which has been so interesting over the last four or five years.
turns.zh: 所以我们会看到大量的人和大量的产品进入市场，很多发行方和很多产品来帮助大家理解市场的新动态、更精准地获取信息，来构建组合——甚至只是应对波动性——过去四五年的波动真的很值得关注。

turns.en: It definitely has been. And certainly of late, Priya, final word to you on that. Sure, I would completely concur. I think people have been underinvested in fixed income for 25 years because there was very little income and you had this massive bull run in the equity market and sort of rates weren't doing anything.
turns.zh: 确实如此。最近尤其明显。Priya，这个话题最后交给你来收尾。好的，我完全同意。我觉得人们有 25 年都在低配固定收益，因为收益太少、股市又有巨大的牛市，利率也几乎没有什么波动。

turns.en: And now you look at portfolios. Number one, there's a lot of equity exposure. So you may want to start to build some balance and there's a huge AI exposure.
turns.zh: 现在你看各类组合：第一，股票敞口很大，所以你可能想开始建立一些平衡；第二，有巨大的 AI 敞口。

turns.en: And what fixed income gives you is this diversified set of returns. It's not just an AI trade or a tech trade. You have the treasury trade. You have credit outside of AI.
turns.zh: 而固定收益给你的是一组多元化的回报来源。不只是 AI 主线或科技主线——你有国债交易，有 AI 以外的信用。

turns.en: And so I think as investors say, we need to rebalance and maybe reduce some of our equity or concentration in the equity portfolio in AI, we can start to look at things.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得当投资者说我们需要再平衡、也许该降低一些股票或 AI 的集中度时，我们就可以开始看看这些机会了。

turns.en: And that's what I think being thoughtful about is this for income? Do I need diversification? At what point does something break and I want liquidity?
turns.zh: 这才是我觉得需要认真思考的：是为了收益吗？我需要分散化吗？什么时候会出问题、我需要流动性？

turns.en: I think fixed income can also provide you if you're in public fixed income. It's a highly liquid asset class that's likely to be if you don't take duration risk likely to be pretty safe.
turns.zh: 我觉得如果你持有的是公开市场固定收益，它也可以提供这些功能——它是一个高流动性资产类别，如果你不承担久期风险的话，它大概率是相当安全的。

turns.en: I think there's a fixed income fund for everyone. And I think that the industry started waking up and sort of developing that. That does it for ETF edge the podcast.
turns.zh: 我觉得每个人都有一只适合自己的固定收益基金。我认为行业正在觉醒并去开发这些产品。好了，本期 ETF Edge 播客就到这里。

turns.en: Thanks for listening. Join us again next week or head to ETF edge dot CMBC dot com.
turns.zh: 感谢收听。下周再见，或者访问 ETF Edge 的官网 ETF Edge 点 CNBC 点 com。
